blocks.text: Good morning Cynthia,

You asked whether we can give you a read on any of the surviving marks before the formal report. Not yet, and I will not guess at it. The full clearance search is running on all the survivors at once, and until it closes I have hits to log, not a view to hand you.

What I can promise is that a head-on collision does not wait for the report. If the search turns up a mark that plainly blocks one of the candidates Jackson Inc gave us, you will hear it from me the day it surfaces. The considered read on the rest, mark by mark, comes in the written report, after counsel has reviewed it.

Our contact record still shows Cynthia Hunter as the single approver for the {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} clearance, so anything that needs a decision comes to you first. Kelly Snyder is logging every hit against the docket as the search returns them, so nothing slips between the search and the report.

One thing would help. If your board has a date in view for this decision, send it to me, and I will tell you plainly whether the report can be ready before it or whether we should plan a short interim note in the meantime.
Regards

This session reviewed the progress of the full clearance search and settled the shape of the written report. It was a working meeting between the firm's prosecution team and the client. It reached no conclusion on the risk of any candidate mark; that view comes in the report, after counsel has reviewed it. These minutes record what was covered and what was assigned.
In Attendance
Discussion

Ashley Williams reported on the full clearance search. It is running on all surviving candidates at once, against the federal register, the state registries, and the common-law sources the firm can reach. Running the sources in parallel keeps the search from stretching out one source at a time. It is partway through, and hits are logged against each candidate as they return. None has been assessed for risk.

The count of hits is not itself a signal. A mark can draw many near matches and clear, or draw few and not. Ashley Williams kept the record to what the searches returned, not to what they might mean, which is the discipline the report depends on. The risk read waits until every source on a mark is in.

Kelly Snyder reported the docket status. Every candidate, every class, and every hit sits in one search file. Each search carries a check date, so no search can drift past the point where it should be revisited. The record is current as of this session, and the docket is the source of truth for it, not anyone's notes.

The candidates that dropped at the knockout stage remain dropped, and the file notes why each fell. The substitute mark Jackson Inc submitted is in the full search with the survivors, so it clears on the same pass. No candidate has been added or removed since the last update.

Cynthia Hunter raised two practical concerns from the client side: the report's timing against the board's calendar, and whether the firm can flag a clear problem early. Ashley Williams answered that the search is on schedule for the report, and that a head-on collision would be reported the day it surfaced. She repeated that no considered risk view precedes the written report and counsel's review.

On timing, the group did not fix a delivery date, because the report follows the close of the searches and the searches are not closed. Ashley Williams offered a short interim note if the board needs something before the full report is ready. Cynthia Hunter will send the board's timing so the firm can choose between the two. Neither option changes the substance of the clearance.

The group settled the shape of the written report. It will be organized by candidate mark, one section each, so the client can read it against the marks it cares about most first. Kelly Snyder will assemble it from the search record once the searches close, and counsel will review the read on the risk before it goes out.

items: For each surviving mark, the conflicts the search turned up.
For each surviving mark, the firm's read of the risk it carries.
For each surviving mark, the options that read leaves open to Jackson Inc.
A short note on the sources searched and the date the search closed, so the scope of the clearance is on the record.

blocks.text: The next session follows the close of the searches. Its purpose will be to read the draft report before it reaches the client. Nothing before then needs a decision from Cynthia Hunter beyond the board timing noted above.
Status Report: Trademark Clearance for Jackson Inc
Prepared by Ashley Williams, Patent Agent, for {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}}. This report covers the current period and is written against the search record, candidate by candidate.
Where We Stand

We are at the midpoint of the clearance, and the work is where it should be. The full search on the surviving candidate marks is well advanced, the docket is current, and nothing in the engagement is behind.
Nothing needs a decision from you this period. One decision touches your side, the report's timing against your board, and it is described below so you have it in view before it arrives.
Who Is On It

The team that started the clearance is the team still on it. I run the searches and the analysis, and I am your day-to-day contact on the substance of the work. Kelly Snyder holds the search record and the docket, and she will build the written report from what the searches return. Anything that turns on a judgment about risk is reviewed by counsel before it reaches you.
What We Did This Period

The work this period was the full clearance search on the marks that survived the knockout stage. We ran it on all of them together, across the federal register, the state registries, and the common-law sources, so that no one candidate waited behind another.

items: We searched every surviving candidate against all three source sets and logged each hit against the mark it touches.
We folded the substitute mark Jackson Inc added into the same pass, so it clears with the survivors and not on a later one.
Kelly Snyder kept the search record current and anchored to the docket, with a check date on every search so none can drift.
We confirmed that the candidates dropped at the knockout stage stay dropped, and that no candidate has been added or removed since.

blocks.text: A word on what the hits mean, since a raw count invites the wrong reading. A candidate can draw many near matches and still clear, or draw only a few and not. The number is not the signal; the analysis is, and that is the work of the next period.
What Comes Next

The next period completes the searches and turns the record into the written clearance report. The report is organized by candidate mark, one section each, so you can read it against the marks that matter most to you first.

items: We finish the remaining searches on the survivors and close the record.
Kelly Snyder assembles the written report from that record, mark by mark.
Counsel reviews the read on the risk each mark carries before the report reaches you.
We deliver the report, and I flag anything in it that needs a decision from you as it comes up.

blocks.text: The report will set out, for each surviving mark, the conflicts the search turned up, our read of the risk it carries, and the options that read leaves open. Where a conflict is close enough that reasonable people could weigh it differently, we will say so plainly, not resolve it more firmly than the record allows.
Risks

There is no finding to report this period, and so no risk that turns on one. The standing limit on any clearance is the reach of the search itself: it covers the marks and classes we cleared and the records our sources reach as of the date we report, and no further.

If the search turns up a mark that plainly blocks one of the candidates, you will hear it from me the day it surfaces, not first in the report. The same holds for anything that would widen the work beyond the scope we agreed. You will not learn of a problem from a status report for the first time.
Budget

The engagement fee is {{fact:f:E-2024-001.fee}}, fixed for the scope we agreed, and the work is tracking within it. At the midpoint we have used a little under half of that amount, which is where a clearance of this shape should sit at this stage.

If anything would take the work past that fee, we will tell you and price it before we begin, not fold it into the number you agreed to. Widening the search beyond the marks, classes, or territory we scoped is the one thing that would do it, and none of that has come up.

We will send the next report at the usual interval, and if the searches close before then, you will have the written clearance report itself in that window. Call me if anything here needs more than a report can give.
